summary: Learn supplier due diligence, risk-tiering, contract controls, monitoring, and escalation. Build a practical third-party risk programme today.
lede: Third-party risk management for procurement and vendor ecosystems helps you identify, assess, treat, monitor, and report risks from external providers. The course focuses on supplier segmentation, risk-based due diligence, control mapping, performance monitoring, and documented incident escalation across operational, financial, compliance, cybersecurity, and reputational risk. You will turn procurement data, contract obligations, audit findings, and incidents into practical tools, including a risk taxonomy, tiering model, due diligence scorecard, control-mapped contract schedules, Power BI monitoring view, and escalation workflow. Exercises address incomplete data, limited review capacity, fragmented ownership, inconsistent evidence, budget pressure, and business resistance while introducing ISO 31000, COSO ERM, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0, and the Shared Assessments SIG questionnaire.
audienceIntro: This third-party risk management training is designed for professionals who assess, govern, procure, monitor, audit, or sponsor external service relationships. It suits intermediate practitioners who already work with suppliers, contracts, controls, audits, or operational services and need a coordinated risk programme. This course is designed for: Procurement Managers who segment suppliers and embed risk criteria into sourcing. Contract Managers who maintain obligations, remedies, and control schedules. Third-Party Risk Analysts who perform due diligence and calculate risk scores. Compliance Officers who map supplier controls to regulatory and policy requirements. Internal Auditors who test vendor governance and evidence quality. Risk Managers who integrate external-party exposures into enterprise risk registers. Operations Leaders who oversee outsourced services and continuity dependencies. Information Security Managers who assess supplier cyber controls and incident readiness. Business Continuity Managers who evaluate critical-provider recovery capabilities. Fraud Risk Specialists who investigate vendor conflicts, misconduct, and payment anomalies.
prerequisites: You should have working exposure to procurement, supplier management, contract administration, compliance, internal audit, enterprise risk, information security, business continuity, or operational service delivery. No programming is required. Basic familiarity with spreadsheets, risk registers, contracts, and control evidence will help you complete the exercises effectively.
